angularDiameterSource: No angular diameter is measured: this is the record's radius at the Gaia distance.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 source 6843672087120107264: parallax 24.5275 +/- 0.0354 mas (RUWE 1.12), inverted to 40.7705 pc with no zero-point correction.
radiusSource: Temperature 6554 +29/-27 K from the BT-NextGen fit to the star's spectral energy distribution by Kral et al. (2026, A&A 705, A217; arXiv:2511.20091) and mass 1.31 +0.03/-0.02 solar masses from their joint orbit fit (Table 2). No paper used here gives a radius, so it is Gaia DR3's FLAME value, 1.3727 solar radii (Creevey et al. 2023), a catalogue model value from Gaia's photometry and parallax, not a measured disc: 954,963 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. GM from 1.31 solar masses times the JPL solar GM. presentationUp: the display axis (celestial north at the star) is up; no spin axis is measured on the sky.
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/hd-206893.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.280, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius. The star's disc is not resolved; its colour is Gaia's spectrum of it.
